package_info.why_malicious: No malicious package is described in this report. The incident involves abuse of compromised OAuth tokens to access private repositories and infrastructure, not the distribution of a malicious package.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains OAuth tokens for Heroku and Travis-CI applications.
attack_chain.leads_to: Use of tokens to access private repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen OAuth tokens to enumerate and download private repositories from victim organizations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential extraction of sensitive information from repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to an AWS API key from downloaded data and uses it to access npm production infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential further compromise of npm infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual OAuth token usage from unexpected locations
Access to production infrastructure using previously unseen AWS API keys
network_indicators: OAuth token authentication from anomalous IPs
Large data transfers from private repository endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for OAuth tokens being used from unfamiliar IP addresses or geographies, especially for bulk repository downloads. Alert on access to production infrastructure using AWS API keys that have not been seen before or are associated with recently accessed repositories. Correlate OAuth token usage with known application IDs (Heroku, Travis-CI) and look for anomalous patterns.
